input.user_message: I need to pick fonts for my upcoming album artwork, website, and press releases. What are some best practices for establishing typography standards for my artist brand?

expected.output_sample:
Establishing clear typography standards is a crucial element of your artist brand's visual identity, as fonts convey mood, genre, and professionalism just as much as colors or imagery. (Mode A) Your chosen fonts will appear across all your visual communications, from the subtle details on your album liner notes to prominent headlines on your website. Consistent typography ensures readability, maintains a cohesive brand aesthetic, and reinforces recognition, making your brand feel polished and thoughtfully designed. Inconsistent fonts can create a cluttered or amateurish impression.

(Mode B) Start by selecting 2-3 font families: a primary display font for titles/logos (that captures your unique style), a secondary font for subheadings/short texts, and a clear, highly readable body font for longer paragraphs (e.g., press releases, website text). For your indie-rock album, you might pair a bold, slightly distressed sans-serif for titles with a clean, modern serif for body text. Ensure your chosen fonts are licensed for commercial use across all intended applications (print, web, merch). (Mode B continued) Document your font choices, including specific weights (e.g., Light, Regular, Bold), sizes for different uses (e.g., H1: 48px, Body: 16px), and line spacing. Provide these specifications to your designers and web developers. Google Fonts and Adobe Fonts offer excellent libraries with robust licensing. I'll coordinate with our <<<CREATIVE>>> specialist to help you explore font pairings that align with your genre and brand vision.

(Mode C) Remember, readability is paramount, especially for digital media. While a unique display font can add character, ensure your body text is comfortable to read. This thoughtful approach to typography will elevate your brand's overall presentation, making it easier for your audience to engage with your story and music. Don't be afraid to experiment with pairings, but always prioritize clarity and consistency.
